name: Stopping helps
why: 4: two runs of 1 cost (1 + 1) + (1 + 1); one run of 2 costs 4 + 1 = 5.

name: Stopping costs too much
why: 14: one run, 4 + 10. Two runs would cost 22.

name: Free stops
why: 22: with c = 0, stopping everywhere is best: 4 + 1 + 16 + 1.

name: Five stations
why: 20: stop at 3; each run is 2 long, costing 4 + 6.

name: Far apart
why: 999,999² + 1,000,000 = 999,999,000,001. The numbers grow large: Python's whole numbers hold them exactly.

name: 150,000 stations
show: 150,000 stations at random rising positions up to 7.5 × 10⁸, c = 10⁹
why: Trying every earlier stop is about 10¹⁰ steps. Lines in a deque take O(n).

name: Even spacing
why: Evenly spaced stops make many crossing points equal. Remove a line when the new one passes under at the same place or earlier (≤), and compare with whole numbers.

name: Long runs between stops
why: Stops are expensive, so the best runs are about 31,600 long, over 10,000 stations each. Looking back only a fixed number of stations fails here.
